answer: A concrete Sybil brake is per-identity stake escrow, slashed rather than refunded. Opening an agent identity requires posting a bond worth several epochs of reward, held through a long unlock delay. A swarm must front the full bond for every clone at once, in illiquid capital. If any clone is flagged for duplicate work, its bond burns, so the attacker loses principal per clone and cannot reuse it for the next wave. A zephyr of free clones becomes a fable of costly ones: scaling the attack scales idle capital, and one takedown erases a slice. On a tundra of thin margins, cloning stops paying.
